# Appeal of Denied Prior Authorization — Request for Reconsideration

**Date:** [Date you send this letter]

**To:** UnitedHealthcare — Appeals
Submit online at member.uhc.com, or call the number on my member ID card. I am also sending this to the appeal address printed on my denial letter, as that letter instructs.

**From:**
Quinn Grant
[Street address]
[City, State ZIP]
[Phone number]

**RE: Appeal of adverse benefit determination dated 2026-08-02**
- **Member:** Quinn Grant
- **Member ID:** W553544386
- **Reference number:** POC-87E365CAED-66145
- **Service denied:** ACL reconstruction, CPT 29888
- **Plan:** UnitedHealthcare, Commercial/ACA, State of Minnesota
- **Governing policy:** *Surgery of the Knee (Commercial)* — https://www.uhcprovider.com/content/dam/provider/docs/public/policies/comm-medical-drug/surgery-knee.pdf

---

Dear Appeals Reviewer,

I am appealing the denial of prior authorization for my ACL reconstruction (CPT 29888). The denial notice dated 2026-08-02 states that the clinical records submitted do not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment before surgery. I am asking UnitedHealthcare to reconsider that decision. My records do document conservative treatment, and my surgeon, Dr. Duval, has documented that this surgery is needed.

I am filing within the timeframe the plan itself set: my notice states the appeal must be received within 180 days of the date of the notice, by **2027-01-29**.

## The plan's own policy, and what it does and does not say

The medical policy identified above, *Surgery of the Knee (Commercial)*, states:

> "Coverage Rationale Surgery of the knee is proven and medically necessary in certain circumstances."

The same policy then directs the reader elsewhere for the actual standards:

> "For medical necessity clinical coverage criteria, refer to the InterQual® CP:"

and confirms:

> "UnitedHealthcare may also use tools developed by third parties, such as the InterQual® criteria, to assist us in administering health benefits."

This matters to my appeal. The excerpts of the policy available to me do not contain any stated requirement for a specific duration, number of visits, or type of conservative care before ACL reconstruction. **I am not aware of any published plan language setting such a threshold, and I have not been given one.** The excerpt quoted above ends in a colon and points to criteria held in a separate, licensed product that I cannot read. I therefore cannot tell what standard my records were measured against, or how they were found to fall short of it. I say plainly that no plan language establishing a conservative-care threshold has been quoted to me, and I am not going to guess at one.

I also note that several passages in this policy address procedures that are not the procedure I am requesting. For example, the policy states:

> "Articular cartilage repair is unproven and not medically necessary for treating individuals with any of the following due to insufficient evidence of efficacy:"

and, in discussing a different device and technique:

> "The authors concluded that there are no data available that support the superiority or equality of TruFit compared with conservative treatment or mosaicplasty/microfracture."

and, elsewhere:

> "these criteria apply to meniscal allografts."

My requested surgery is ACL reconstruction. It is not articular cartilage repair and it is not a meniscal allograft. The policy excerpt beginning "Articular cartilage repair is unproven..." ends in a colon and introduces a list of conditions that was not reproduced in the material available to me; I am not able to see that list, and I ask the plan to identify exactly which criteria it applied to my request.

## What my records actually document

Whatever threshold the plan applied, here is what is in my chart:

| What the records show | Detail as documented |
|---|---|
| Symptom duration | 24 months of progressive knee pain, unrelieved by rest |
| Supervised physical therapy | Range of motion and quadriceps strengthening, with bracing — 10 weeks, 2026-04-12 to 2026-06-21, **20 visits completed**, documented in the physical therapy discharge note |
| Medication trial | NSAIDs for 6 months, with inadequate relief |
| Injection | Corticosteroid injection on 2026-04-17, giving 3 weeks of partial relief |
| Imaging (2026-06-29) | MRI of the knee: complete mid-substance tear of the anterior cruciate ligament with bone bruise pattern; menisci intact; no significant arthritis |
| Function | Recurrent instability with pivoting; knee has given way twice on stairs |
| Exam | Positive provocative testing on the affected side; range of motion limited by pain |
| Surgical risk factors | No active infection, no untreated substance use, BMI 29, non-smoker |

This is a completed, supervised, and documented course of non-surgical care across three separate modalities — therapy, bracing, and medication, including an injection — over months, followed by imaging showing a complete tear of the ligament. The denial states my records do not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment. The records above are the trial. If the plan's position is that this course of care was still not adequate, I am asking the plan to state in writing what would have been adequate, and where that requirement is written down.

The policy also states:

> "Medical records documentation may be required to assess whether the member meets the clinical criteria for coverage but does not guarantee coverage of the service requested;"

I understand that submitting records does not by itself guarantee coverage. I am not asking for coverage on the basis of paperwork alone. I am asking that the records I did submit be measured against a criterion that is identified to me, because the reason given for the denial is the one thing my records do document.

## Request for the criteria applied to my determination

**I am requesting, in writing and free of charge, the specific rule, guideline, protocol, or criterion that UnitedHealthcare relied on to deny this request.** Because the governing policy directs reviewers to InterQual, I am specifically asking for **the InterQual subset, edition, and full criteria text applied to my determination**, along with the credentials and specialty of the reviewer who made the decision. Federal ERISA and ACA appeal rules require the plan to provide the specific rule or criterion relied on for an adverse determination at no cost to me. The plan holds these criteria; I do not, and I cannot meaningfully respond to a standard I have never been shown.

## What I am asking for

I ask UnitedHealthcare to:

1. Overturn the denial of prior authorization for ACL reconstruction, CPT 29888, and approve the procedure;
2. Provide me the InterQual subset, edition, and full criteria text applied to my determination, and the reviewer's credentials;
3. Identify which specific criterion in *Surgery of the Knee (Commercial)*, or in the criteria it incorporates, my records were found not to meet; and
4. Have this appeal reviewed by a physician in orthopedic surgery who has read the physical therapy discharge note and the 2026-06-29 MRI report.

Please contact me at [phone number] or [email address] if any additional records would help. I am happy to have Dr. Duval's office send anything further, and I authorize my treating providers to discuss my care with your reviewers.

Thank you for taking a careful second look at this.

Sincerely,

**Quinn Grant**
Member ID: W553544386
Reference number: POC-87E365CAED-66145
[Signature]
[Date]

**Enclosures:**
- Copy of the denial notice dated 2026-08-02
- Physical therapy discharge note, 2026-04-12 to 2026-06-21 (20 visits)
- MRI report, 2026-06-29
- Office notes from Dr. Duval, orthopedic surgery
- Medication and injection records, including corticosteroid injection 2026-04-17
- [Any additional records your provider's office is sending]

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
